title: Integral Cartier blowups of the reduced components of a proper pair
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $T$ be a nonempty reduced proper finite-type $e$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $C\subseteq T$ be nowhere dense and closed. The irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $T$ admit a finite nonempty enumeration $T_1,\ldots,T_s$, each equipped with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Each $T_i$ is nonempty integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and proper over $e$. Write $C_i=C\cap T_i$ with its reduced induced structure and $\mathcal I_i$ for its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. This ideal is quasi-coherent of finite type, and $U_i=T_i\setminus C_i$ is nonempty, quasi-compact and dense. The ordinary blowup $b_i:S_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}T_i\to T_i$ [def-nagata-global-blowup] is proper and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], $S_i$ is a nonempty integral proper finite-type $e$-scheme, and $b_i^{-1}U_i\to U_i$ is an isomorphism with $b_i^{-1}U_i$ dense in $S_i$. In particular $b_i$ is birational, meaning it identifies dense open subschemes, and identifies the function fields [def-sc-function-field]. The extended ideal $\mathcal I_i\mathcal O_{S_i}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], with support $b_i^{-1}C_i$. If $C_i$ is empty, $\mathcal I_i=\mathcal O_{T_i}$ and $b_i$ is the identity.

proof.text: The field $e$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $(1)$, both finitely generated. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}e$ is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact (its space has one point). Apply finite type over a Noetherian base to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}e$. The scheme $T$ is Noetherian and hence has finitely many irreducible components. These components cover $T$; since $T$ is nonempty, their finite set is nonempty. Choose an enumeration $|T_1|,\ldots,|T_s|$.

Give each closed component its reduced induced closed subscheme structure. It is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by the characterization of integrality. Its closed immersion into $T$ makes it proper over $e$; in particular its structure morphism is of finite type, so it too is Noetherian. Apply the reduced-induced-subscheme construction inside $T_i$ to the closed subset $C\cap|T_i|$, obtaining $C_i$ and its quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_i$.

source.place: Tags 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), 01J4 (definition-reduced-induced-scheme); properties.tex Tag 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral); morphisms.tex Tags 01W5 and 01T6

proof.text: No component is contained in $C$. Indeed, for fixed $i$ put $O_i=T\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}|T_j|$. The components cover $T$, so $O_i\subseteq|T_i|$. It is nonempty: otherwise $|T_i|$ would be a finite union of its closed intersections with the other components, so irreducibility would force containment in one other component, contrary to maximality and distinctness. If $|T_i|\subseteq C$, the nonempty open $O_i$ would be contained in $C$, contradicting nowhere density. Therefore $U_i=T_i\setminus C_i$ is nonempty and dense, since every nonempty open in an irreducible space is dense (two disjoint nonempty opens would give a union of two proper closed subsets).

source.place: Tag 0052 (lemma-Noetherian), component-open argument; the finite union and density arguments are written out

proof.text: The open subscheme $U_i$ of the Noetherian scheme $T_i$ is Noetherian and in particular quasi-compact. Take a Noetherian affine open covering of $T_i$. On each member $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the ideal $\mathcal I_i(V)$ is finitely generated by the definition of a Noetherian ring. The affine finite-type criterion for quasi-coherent modules now makes $\mathcal I_i$ of finite type. It is nonzero: if it were zero, its affine vanishing sets would be all of $T_i$, whereas its vanishing set is $C_i$ and $U_i$ is nonempty.

Form the ordinary blowup $b_i:S_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}(T_i)\to T_i$. Apply integral-blowup geometry using the nonzero quasi-coherent finite-type ideal established above; it gives that $S_i$ is integral, in particular nonempty. The global blowup properness theorem makes $b_i$ proper. The complement theorem identifies $b_i^{-1}U_i$ with $U_i$. This inverse image is a nonempty open in the integral (hence irreducible) scheme $S_i$, and is therefore dense by the two-open argument of step 3.

The image of $b_i$ is closed because proper morphisms are universally closed; it contains $U_i$ by the complement isomorphism, so density of $U_i$ makes the image all of $T_i$. This is surjectivity. Compose $b_i$ with the proper structure morphism $T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}e$. Proper composition gives that $S_i$ is proper over $e$, and finite type is part of the definition of proper. This proves all finiteness, nonemptiness and properness assertions for $S_i$.

source.place: Tag 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper); surjectivity is the elementary closed-image argument

proof.text: The complement isomorphism identifies dense opens on both integral schemes, which is the stated meaning of birationality. By sobriety each has a unique generic point, and both generic points belong to these dense opens. The isomorphism of opens identifies these points and their structure-sheaf stalks: restriction to an open neighbourhood does not change a stalk, since neighbourhoods inside that open are cofinal among all neighbourhoods. The resulting isomorphism $\mathcal O_{T_i,\eta_i}\simeq\mathcal O_{S_i,\xi_i}$ is the function-field identification $k(T_i)\simeq k(S_i)$, with both rings fields by the generic-stalk theorem.

Principalization applies to the finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_i$ and says that its extended ideal on $S_i$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor, hence is an effective Cartier ideal. To check the support, use the extended-ideal definition and the closed-subscheme base-change ideal formula: this is the ideal of $C_i\times_{T_i}S_i$. Affine-locally, if $A\to B$ represents $b_i$ and $J\subseteq A$ defines $C_i$, that ideal is $JB$. A prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ contains $JB$ exactly when its inverse-image prime in $A$ contains $J$. The affine ideal-zero-set formula therefore gives precisely $V(\mathcal I_i\mathcal O_{S_i})=b_i^{-1}|C_i|$.

source.place: Tag 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor); affine base-change formula for closed immersions

proof.text: If $C_i=\varnothing$, the reduced-induced ideal is the unit ideal: its sections are the functions vanishing at all points of the empty set, a vacuous condition. Now $U_i=T_i$, so the complement isomorphism is the entire map $b_i:S_i\to T_i$. It identifies the blowup canonically with $T_i$ and $b_i$ with its identity. The extended unit ideal defines the empty effective Cartier divisor, consistently with the preceding step.
